title: Surrogates with fixed month distributions did not reproduce six-month Nino 3.4 change asymmetry in 1950-2025
abstract: We tested whether calendar-month distributions can reproduce a previously reported six-month temperature change asymmetry. We used 912 NOAA CPC ERSSTv5 Nino 3.4 monthly anomalies for 1950-2025. The normalized cubic change statistic was -0.5066. None of 999 surrogate records with fixed calendar-month distributions had a larger absolute statistic. The nominal tail fraction was 0.001. A pooled comparison also gave 0.001. However, the month constraints increased median Fourier amplitude error from 0.44% to 5.84%. The 1950-1987 test gave 0.182; the 1988-2025 test gave 0.002. This supplies a seasonal distribution benchmark for a pattern selected on the same data. It does not test all seasonal linear models or establish a physical cause. The method does not preserve month-specific transition covariance, and its tail fractions are not calibrated probabilities. Source error, nonstationarity, approximate spectral fit and prior selection limit inference. The package includes original code, source hashes, scalar simulations, checks and a figure. External monthly data stay outside the bundle.

display.caption: Red diamonds show observed cubic change statistics. Blue bars show central 95% surrogate ranges. White points show medians. The nominal absolute tail fraction is p*. These ranges are not confidence intervals. The right panel shows median to maximum Fourier amplitude error. Month constraints retain empirical month distributions exactly but weaken the spectral fit.

citations.reason: Published evidence and its seasonal limit set the question, source and statistic. We wrote new code. Source observations overlap; this is not independent confirmation.
Original campaign report of the selected six-month change pattern.
Iterative Fourier amplitude and rank adjustment method; no third-party code is included.
